newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS-Telefonica/MCI seen on verge of Americas deal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Telefonica/MCI seen on verge of Americas deal.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica de Espana may be on the verge of forming an alliance with U.S.-based MCI which would catapult it into the ranks of the world's biggest telecommunications groupings.
In a confusing turn of events, Portugal Telecom, which has apparently had no direct part in the talks, leaked word on Monday that Telefonica and MCI had reached a deal.
Telefonica and MCI denied an announcement was imminent, but made no statement about the status of their ongoing discussions.
It all started when Portugal Telecom, in announcing its own deal with MCI and British Telecom, made a brief reference to an accord that it said Telefonica and MCI had already made public.

"Portugal Telecom, MCI and BT will also explore opportunities to work together in Latin America through the Pan American joint venture announced today by MCI and Telefonica Internacional," Portugal Telecom said.
But Telefonica and MCI had not made any announcement.
Portugal Telecom had no part in Telefonica-MCI discussions, but the Lisbon-based company may have learned of an impending deal through its own business links with MCI and BT.
While Portugal Telecom's announcement may have been premature, analysts said they still expected a deal between the two in the near future.
"Of all the possible alliances between Telefonica and a U.S. operator, the most probable is MCI," said an analyst at a Spanish brokerage.

Telefonica denied it would sign an accord with MCI today, adding that it was still discussing an alliance with AT&T, with whom it already has a European alliance, as well as with BT and MCI, who are merging into Concert.

"Telefonica categorically denies the information published this morning by various international news agencies, dated in Lisbon, announcing the signing today of an agreement between Telefonica Internacional and MCI," Telefonica said in a brief statement.

From Lisbon, MCI said the Portugal Telecom reference to a venture with Telefonica was an 'error', but left unclear whether the error was one of inclusion, of signing, or of a deal. It said it would make no announcement on any venture today.

Telefonica, which is more than halfway through its self-imposed deadline of six weeks to select a U.S. partner, said it would not be rushed into a decision, but analysts said they thought it was moving ahead on a likely alliance with MCI.

"Alliances are a very sensitive subject and when somebody jumps the gun on talks one has to deny it categorically and I think it is very good that Telefonica did so," another Madrid-based analyst said.

Telefonica hopes to use its strong Latin American presence to help it into an alliance that will open up the huge U.S. Spanish speaking market and vault the group into the ranks of the top global telecommunications groups.

Telefonica wants privileged access to the 40 million Spanish speakers in the United States, and in return offers a ticket into Latin America, where it -- through Telefonica Internacional (TISA) -- had sales last year of some 350 billion pesetas ($2.4 billion).
TISA participates in the management of some 10 million service lines in Latin America, has 984,000 mobile phone clients
